title: Seeds gathered
summary: They had gathered seeds of every kind, including grain and fruit.

title: Lehi recounts his vision
summary: While tarrying in the wilderness, Lehi tells his sons he has seen a vision. He says he rejoices concerning Nephi and Sam and fears for Laman and Lemuel.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi tarried in the wilderness and spoke to his sons, saying he had dreamed a dream or seen a vision.
Lehi said he had reason to rejoice in the Lord because of Nephi and Sam, and supposed they and many of their seed would be saved.
Lehi said he feared exceedingly for Laman and Lemuel and had seen a dark and dreary wilderness in his dream.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi speaks to his sons; his vision may be represented as an imagined image rather than as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: The sons' reactions and attire; the wilderness's specific appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I have dreamed a dream;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

spoken_dialogue.text: or, in other words, I have seen a vision.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

narration.text: because of the thing which I have seen, I have reason to rejoice in the Lord because of Nephi and also of Sam;
But behold, Laman and Lemuel, I fear exceedingly because of you;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi reports his dream or vision to his sons.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the vision wilderness as a present event or place the sons inside it.

title: The white-robed man
summary: The narrator sees a man dressed in a white robe. The man comes and stands before the narrator, then speaks and bids the narrator to follow him.

The man came and stood before the narrator.
The man spoke to the narrator and bade the narrator to follow him.

unspecified_visual_details: The man's identity, face, age, and appearance beyond his white robe.
The narrator's appearance and the surroundings.

narration.text: I saw a man, and he was dressed in a white robe;
and he came and stood before me.
and bade me follow him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not identify the man or quote his speech directly.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the man as an angel or assign him a name.

summary: Lehi follows the man and finds himself in a dark and dreary waste. After traveling many hours in darkness, he prays for mercy.

explicit_facts.text: As Lehi followed the man, he found himself in a dark and dreary waste.
After traveling many hours in darkness, Lehi prayed to the Lord for mercy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Darkness obscures the waste around Lehi.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, time of day, and whether the man remains visible.

title: A spacious field and a tree

reasonable_visual_inferences: The tree may be shown in the field.
unspecified_visual_details: The narrator’s appearance, tree species, fruit appearance, and field landscape.

narration.text: I beheld a large and spacious field.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state that the fruit was desirable to make one happy; they do not explain its meaning.

title: Lehi tastes the fruit
summary: Lehi takes and eats the tree's fruit. He finds it exceedingly sweet and white, and desires that his family partake because it fills him with great joy.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi went forth and partook of the fruit.
He found the fruit sweeter than anything he had tasted and whiter than anything he had seen.
The fruit filled Lehi's soul with great joy, and he desired that his family partake of it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi holds and eats a white fruit.
unspecified_visual_details: Fruit species, shape, and size; how joy is visually expressed.

narration.text: it was most sweet,

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the fruit a specific species or add symbolic interpretation.

title: The river and its head
summary: The narrator recounts looking around for his family and seeing a river running near the tree. Looking toward the river's head a little way off, he saw Sariah, Sam, and Nephi standing as if they did not know where to go.
locations: The tree and nearby river described in the account
The river's head a little way off

explicit_facts.text: The narrator looked around, hoping to discover his family.
The narrator saw a river running near the tree.
The narrator looked toward the river's origin and saw its head a little way off.
Sariah, Sam, and Nephi were at the river's head, standing as if they did not know where to go.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Standing figures with no clear directional movement could convey the uncertainty described in the account.
unspecified_visual_details: The river's width and the appearance of its head
The tree's appearance
The people's ages, clothing, and physical appearances
Exact distances and surrounding terrain
The setting in which the narrator recounts these events

narration.text: And as I cast my eyes round about, that perhaps I might discover my family also,
And I looked to behold from whence it came;
and they stood as if they knew not whither they should go.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Preserve the retrospective account rather than staging a new present-tense encounter.
The phrase “as if” describes apparent uncertainty, not confirmed thoughts or motives.
The supplied verses do not identify the narrator by name.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a simultaneous fruit-eating action.
Do not place Sariah, Sam, and Nephi beside the narrator or in an invented storytelling setting.
Do not invent dialogue, gestures, destinations, or reasons for their apparent uncertainty.
Do not invent divine appearances or supernatural properties of the river.

title: Lehi beckons his family
summary: Lehi beckons and calls to Sariah, Sam, and Nephi to come partake of the fruit. They come to him and eat it.

unspecified_visual_details: Their exact route, gestures, and reactions to the fruit.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add dialogue for Sariah, Sam, or Nephi.

title: Looking for Laman and Lemuel
summary: The narrator desires Laman and Lemuel to partake of the fruit, looks toward the head of the river, and sees them. They do not come to him or partake of the fruit.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator desired Laman and Lemuel to come and partake of the fruit and looked toward the head of the river in hopes of seeing them.
The narrator saw Laman and Lemuel, but they would not come to him and partake of the fruit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Laman and Lemuel may be shown apart from the narrator.
unspecified_visual_details: Their expressions, posture, precise positions, and distance from the narrator.

narration.text: And it came to pass that I saw them, but they would not come unto me and partake of the fruit.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the first-person narrator based on these verses alone.
Do not give Laman or Lemuel a motive or spoken refusal.

title: The iron rod and narrow path
summary: The first-person observer beholds an iron rod extending along the riverbank to the tree by which the observer stands. The observer also beholds a strait and narrow path beside the rod that reaches the tree and leads by the head of the fountain to a large and spacious field.

explicit_facts.text: The observer beholds a rod of iron extending along the riverbank and leading to the tree by which the observer stands.
The observer beholds a strait and narrow path beside the rod that reaches the tree.
The path also leads by the head of the fountain to a large and spacious field.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The rod and path can be shown running alongside one another toward the tree.
unspecified_visual_details: The rod's finish and shape, the path's surface, and the landscape's precise layout.

narration.text: And I beheld a rod of iron, and it extended along the bank of the river, and led to the tree by which I stood.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparison of the field to a world is figurative; these verses do not explain the features' symbolism.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the observer a name from outside these verses.
Do not depict the field as a literal world or add a symbolic explanation.

narration.text: And I saw numberless concourses of people,

title: The great and spacious building
summary: A first-person observer beholds a great and spacious building on the other side of the river, high above the earth. People inside mock and point toward those who had come at and were partaking of the fruit.

title: The father's account of scorn
summary: In the father's account, a great multitude entered a strange building and then pointed the finger of scorn at him and those partaking of the fruit. He and the fruit-partakers did not heed them. His words also state that those who heeded them had fallen away.

title: Lehi exhorts Laman and Lemuel
summary: After finishing his vision, Lehi says Laman and Lemuel did not partake of the fruit. He fears for them, exhorts them with parental feeling to heed his words, preaches to them, prophesies many things, and bids them keep the Lord's commandments before ceasing to speak.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi said Laman and Lemuel did not partake of the fruit.
After recounting his vision, Lehi exceedingly feared for Laman and Lemuel, lest they be cast off from the Lord's presence.
Lehi exhorted them with the feeling of a tender parent to heed his words, preached to them, and hoped the Lord would be merciful to them.
After preaching and prophesying many things, Lehi bade them keep the Lord's commandments and ceased speaking.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi speaks to Laman and Lemuel while the family listens.
unspecified_visual_details: The family's arrangement, facial expressions, and the content of the unquoted preaching and prophecies.
